html:
Skill: brain-write — write a doc the brain can use

Use this for any new spec, plan, report, review, experiment, handoff or readme under ~/brain/work/<box>/. Anything is accepted; this format makes it findable, readable one section at a time, and linked to its results.

Start with this header:

---
type: spec            # spec | plan | report | review | experiment | handoff | readme
status: live          # live | draft | superseded | done
summary: one line, ≤ 160 chars — the doc's point, not its topic
hubs: [image-lane]    # 1–3 hub ids: the file names in ~/brain/hubs/
---

Then:

  • One # Title, then ## Sections at H2. Keep each section ≤ ~20 KB: agents read one section, chosen by its summary. Split a section that grows past that.
  • Link to docs and results by relative path (../reports/run-7.md#results, .data/run-7/result.json), so the links become real edges. No absolute paths, no "see the doc in the other folder".
  • Put numbers next to the file that holds them, with a date ("as of 2026-10-08").
  • A new version replaces the old one: name it, set the old one's status: superseded, and keep the old file.
  • STATE.md (where the work stands) stays ≤ 8 KB and is overwritten, never appended to. History goes to log/YYYY-MM-DD.md. CARD.md is written by the dream.
  • Bulk outputs (data, runs, binaries) go under .data/, not next to the docs.

The write guard warns when a new doc lacks the header or has a section over 20 KB, and blocks a STATE.md over 8 KB.
